title: Reading a workflow JSON like a map

questions.q: Which export is the one meant for submitting a graph to a ComfyUI server?
options: File, Save, which keeps positions, sizes and colours
File, Export Workflow (API), which keeps node ids, classes and inputs but no layout
A screenshot of the canvas
The PNG's thumbnail
questions.answer: File, Export Workflow (API), which keeps node ids, classes and inputs but no layout
questions.why: The documentation says the API format omits UI metadata such as positions, colors, groups and node sizes. The server's /prompt route takes that dictionary under the key prompt.

questions.q: In the save-format link row [4, 6, 0, 3, 1, "CONDITIONING"], what does the 3 mean?
options: The id of the link
The slot the link starts from
The id of the node where the link ends
The slot the link ends at
questions.answer: The id of the node where the link ends
questions.why: A link row is [link id, origin node, origin slot, target node, target slot, type]. This row is link 4, from output 0 of node 6 to input 1 of node 3, which is the KSampler's positive input in the lab.

questions.q: The lab's KSampler has 7 widget values but 6 widget inputs in the API format. Which value is missing from the API format?
options: The seed
The "control after generate" choice, which the editor keeps and the server never sees
The sampler name
The denoise value
questions.answer: The "control after generate" choice, which the editor keeps and the server never sees
questions.why: widgets_values is a positional list: seed, control after generate, steps, cfg, sampler_name, scheduler, denoise. The API format has no entry for the second item, as the documented example and the lab's translation show.

questions.q: Why does the lab check the `links` list against each node's own sockets?
options: Because JSON cannot store links
Because the wiring is written twice, so a damaged or hand-edited file can disagree with itself
Because the server requires both lists to be sorted
Because the sockets hold the node positions
questions.answer: Because the wiring is written twice, so a damaged or hand-edited file can disagree with itself
questions.why: Each link appears in the links table and again in the origin node's output socket and the target node's input socket. The lab finds all four planted faults: a deleted row, a wrong slot, a wrong type and a missing node.

questions.q: How does the API format write a wire?
options: As the id of a row in a links table
As a list of two items: the source node's id as a string and the output slot
As the title of the source node
As a row of six items
questions.answer: As a list of two items: the source node's id as a string and the output slot
questions.why: In the documentation's example the KSampler has "model": ["4", 0]. The save format is the one with link rows of six.

questions.q: A hand-written API prompt says "samples": [3, 0] where the node id should be the string "3". What does ComfyUI make of it?
options: It converts the number silently
It runs, using output 0 of whatever node comes first
It does not count as a link, and looking up node 3 fails during validation
It treats it as a LATENT constant
questions.answer: It does not count as a link, and looking up node 3 fails during validation
questions.why: is_link requires a list of two items whose first item is a string. JSON object keys are strings, so the lookup with the number 3 raises a KeyError in validate_inputs, which validate_prompt reports as a failed validation.
